sections.title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
sections.abstract: ScienceIDE turns scientific software repositories into executable environments for task generation, agent interaction, and scientific verification, then uses verified trajectories to train and evaluate scientific coding agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: Infrastructure for converting scientific code into programmable environments for SFT, RL, and evaluation, with reported transfer from PhAI-IDE models.
sections.caveat: The breadth of held-out coverage and the separation of scientific-domain data effects from general data and scale are not established by the abstract.

sections.title: PointZero: 3D Point Track Completion for Learning Transferable 3D Dynamics
sections.abstract: PointZero pretrains a 3D dynamics model by completing sparse point tracks, avoiding robot action labels and enabling transfer to action-conditioned dynamics prediction and imitation learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: A transferable 3D dynamics prior from non-robot data, with reported improvement or parity on 6 of 7 manipulation tasks after fine-tuning.
sections.caveat: Transfer beyond the reported benchmarks and data distribution remains open.

sections.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
sections.abstract: The paper studies whether internal representation directions can detect and discover reward hacking in frontier open-source LLM evaluations, including online prediction of later hacking behavior.
sections.claimed_contribution: Difference-of-means vectors represent and monitor reward hacking, predict some later hacking behavior, and expose behaviors missed by LLM monitors.
sections.caveat: Transfer to other model families, hidden internal states, and adaptive systems is not established.

sections.title: In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents
sections.abstract: GPT-Policy combines a visual context compiler, VLM action proposals, and a constrained controller so robots can adapt from demonstrations and feedback without gradient updates or task-specific parameter changes.
sections.claimed_contribution: A framework for translating VLM capabilities into verifiable physical behavior through context compilation and constrained execution.
sections.caveat: Broad task-family robustness and commercial-model dependence remain unresolved.

sections.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
sections.abstract: Separating tokeniser objective from search procedure, the paper finds bottom-up search usually drives lower bits-per-byte while showing no consistent BLiMP advantage.
sections.claimed_contribution: A 2x2 decomposition of tokeniser design choices, with search procedure dominating bits-per-byte results.
sections.caveat: The conclusions are metric- and setup-dependent.

sections.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
sections.abstract: ComPO is a comparison-based, zeroth-order preference-alignment method that extracts directional information from preference pairs without directly optimising a differentiable preference loss.
sections.claimed_contribution: Offline and online ComPO methods with formal guarantees and reported improvements in length-controlled win rates.
sections.caveat: The guarantees depend on coverage and oracle assumptions whose realism in production preference data is not shown.

sections.title: How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents
sections.abstract: Recursive depth, model growth, and boundary operators can alter pretraining scaling exponents and improve compute efficiency, according to experiments including a 7.4B model comparison with GPT-3 13B.
sections.claimed_contribution: Usable computational depth can produce scale-dependent efficiency gains through looping and related architectural interventions.
sections.caveat: Independent reproduction across architectures, data regimes, and benchmarks is needed.

sections.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
sections.abstract: Adaptive episodic memory and execution-time self-reflection improve a dual-process agent's ScienceWorld score, success rate, and successful-step efficiency.
sections.claimed_contribution: Ablations suggest runtime validation is the dominant bottleneck, with memory becoming more useful after execution control is stabilised.
sections.caveat: The result comes from one benchmark and one agent substrate.
